question: Does the third-moment sign rule account for the exact yaw invariance reported in the merged manuscript, holding the rest of the HeadingNorm construction fixed?
registered_prediction: Without the sign rule the frame is defined modulo pi. Under an input rotation psi the principal axis flips whenever theta+psi crosses pi/2, so the canonicalized input differs and exact invariance fails, as a structured function of the angle rather than uniformly. Accuracy is not predicted to change materially.
primary: per-sequence ATE spread across eight yaw angles
selection: Same 8-subject validation split, same validation windows, Huber loss for checkpoint selection every 2000 steps. No test-based selection. All seeds retained.
